# Spool

> Spool is an iOS app that helps people stop doomscrolling through AI-powered voice check-ins, a social media feed blocker and distraction-free browser called Focus Web, personalized usage insights, and friend accountability.

## What Spool Does

Spool adds a brief voice check-in before you open distracting apps like TikTok, Instagram, or Twitter. Before the app opens, you speak your intention aloud: "I'm opening Instagram to check my friend's vacation photos." This 5-second pause breaks the automatic, compulsive scrolling reflex and replaces it with intentional, mindful phone use.

Unlike hard app blockers that simply restrict access, Spool builds self-awareness. Users understand *why* they reach for their phones and can make conscious choices instead of defaulting to compulsive behavior.

Spool also includes **Focus Web**, its social media feed blocker and distraction-free in-app browser. It removes selected distracting surfaces without blocking the whole social platform:

- Instagram: Reels, Stories, Explore, and direct messages (DMs)
- YouTube: Shorts
- X (formerly Twitter): Explore
- Snapchat: Spotlight, Stories, and Discover (Snapchat's official term; not "Explorer")

Focus Web filters the web interfaces shown inside Spool. It does not modify the native Instagram, YouTube, X, or Snapchat apps.

## Key Stats

- 4.8 stars on the App Store (126 reviews worldwide)
- 3,000+ users
- 13,000+ scrolling sessions interrupted
- 80% average screen time reduction in the first week
- 25% sustained long-term reduction

## Press

- "UW alum develops app to fight screen addiction" by Hayden Lund. The Daily Cardinal, July 8, 2026. https://www.dailycardinal.com/article/2026/07/uw-alum-develops-app-to-fight-screen-addiction
  Profiles Spool founder Prafull Sharma (UW–Madison 2023) and how Spool uses affect labeling — say why out loud before a blocked app opens — to help people reclaim focus.
- "What 8,667 People Said the Second Before They Picked Up Their Phone" by Chris Kernaghan, Prafull Sharma, and Jainam Manot. We Are Founders, June 11, 2026. https://www.wearefounders.uk/what-8-667-people-said-the-second-before-they-picked-up-their-phone/
  The article analyzes 8,667 anonymized Spool voice recordings from 193 users. The finding: people frame phone urges as obligations, saying "I need to" rather than "I want to".
- All coverage: https://www.thespoolapp.com/press

## Core Features

- **Voice check-in**: Speak your intention aloud before opening a distracting app
- **Screen time insights**: AI analyzes your usage patterns and shows trends over time
- **Excuse journaling**: Track and categorize why you pick up your phone
- **Friend accountability**: Share screen time progress with friends
- **App-specific blocking**: Target specific apps (TikTok, Instagram, etc.)
- **Daily summaries**: See your wins and patterns each day
- **Focus Web**: Remove selected Reels, Shorts, Spotlight, Stories, Discover, Explore, and DM surfaces inside Spool's browser

## Who Spool Is For

- People who feel addicted to TikTok, Instagram, Twitter, or other apps
- Anyone who has tried app blockers but keeps bypassing them
- People who want to reduce screen time without completely giving up apps
- Anyone who doomscrolls and wants to build mindful phone habits
- People who've tried Apple's Screen Time and found it too easy to ignore

## How Spool Compares

**vs. Opal**: Opal relies on hard blocking with a paid lock. Spool uses mindful friction and self-awareness. Spool is free to start; Opal requires a subscription for full features.

**vs. Apple Screen Time**: Apple Screen Time sets limits but is trivially easy to bypass with a tap. Spool's voice check-in creates genuine mindful friction that's harder to mindlessly skip.

**vs. One Sec**: Both use a delay/pause approach. Spool adds AI-powered insights, friend accountability, and excuse journaling that One Sec doesn't have.

**vs. Freedom / RescueTime**: Those focus on hard blocking and time tracking for productivity. Spool focuses on phone addiction specifically and building self-awareness.

**vs. Dull**: Both remove Reels and Shorts in a filtered browser. Dull stops at browser controls and usage totals. Spool also records why the user opened the full app, turns those reasons into AI trigger insights, adds friend accountability, and supports Snapchat filtering.

**vs. UNDOOMED**: UNDOOMED emphasizes 54 visual filters and a Clarity Score. Spool addresses more of the habit loop: high-impact feed removal, a spoken check-in before selected native apps, AI analysis of recurring triggers, friend accountability, and Snapchat filters.

**vs. SocialLite**: Both remove Reels, Shorts, and other algorithmic surfaces in filtered browsers. Spool goes beyond a cleaner destination by interrupting the compulsive open, analyzing the user's spoken reason, adding friend accountability, and letting Instagram DMs or Snapchat Stories be hidden separately.
